title: Finora — Reconciliation
description: The two reconciliation counters from ReconciliationMetrics, answering questions the synthetic benchmark in docs/proposals/reconciliation-benchmark/ could not: how often the engine's auto-decisions actually happen in production, and how often a user disagrees with one. This is a measurement dashboard, not an alerting one — there is no established good/bad line for either series yet, so panels are informational rather than threshold-colored. See docs/engineering/observability.md §11.

panels.title: Transfers matched (1h)
panels.description: Auto-matched transfer pairs between a user's own accounts, incremented once per matched pair (matching ReconciliationService's own newTransfers counting convention).

panels.title: Relationship-backed share (1h)
panels.description: Share of matched transfers backed by a stored account relationship rather than the date/amount heuristic alone. Both halves come from the same counter (relationshipMatch=true/false), so this ratio needs no separate denominator — unlike duplicate overrides below.

panels.title: Transfer matches by relationship confidence
panels.description: Best-candidate scoring (ReconciliationService.transferCandidateScore) weighs a relationship match above the date-proximity heuristic. This is the production signal for whether that scoring is actually favoring relationship-backed pairs over time, which the synthetic benchmark cannot observe.

panels.title: Duplicate overrides (1h)
panels.description: A user rejected an auto-flagged duplicate via TransactionService.confirmNotDuplicate — the one user-facing correction that exists today for a wrong reconciliation verdict. There is no auto-flagged-duplicate counter yet, so this has no rate/denominator to divide by (a documented gap, not an omission here).

panels.title: Duplicate overrides by source
panels.description: Split by the transaction's row source (MANUAL / CSV_IMPORT / GMAIL_IMPORT). A sustained rise from one import source over the others is the earliest production signal that its duplicate-detection heuristic needs attention.
